fish.name: Slate Herring
fish.flavor: The backbone of the fleet's economy and the seagull's diet. Travels in schools so vast the water goes dark, which the herring consider a group accomplishment.

fish.name: Butter Mackerel
fish.flavor: Striped like the tide and rich as its name. Locals fry it in the morning fog and swear it tastes better if you complain about the weather first.

fish.name: Drift Cod
fish.flavor: Follows the currents wherever they wander, which, if you think about it, is also how most of its anglers ended up out here.

fish.name: Weather Whiting
fish.flavor: Bites best in the hour before a squall. Old-timers stopped watching the sky years ago; they watch the whiting bucket.

fish.name: Saltwife Sardine
fish.flavor: Named for the wives who salted them down by the barrelful. One is a snack; a thousand is a winter.

fish.name: Ballast Bream
fish.flavor: Heavy for its size, like it swallowed a pocketful of gravel out of principle. Handy for keeping the catch crate from sliding in high swells.

fish.name: Penny Skipjack
fish.flavor: Flashes copper when it jumps, which it does constantly, joyfully, and for no reason anyone has ever determined.

fish.name: Dogtooth Hake
fish.flavor: All underbite and attitude. Bites the hook mostly out of spite, which the hook appreciates.

fish.name: Old Bootsole
fish.flavor: A flounder so flat and brown that at least three anglers have tried to re-sole a boot with one. It did not work, but the boot smelled interesting for weeks.

fish.name: Brine Scad
fish.flavor: Tastes like the sea, smells like the sea, and is, in most measurable respects, the sea with fins.

fish.name: Rigging Eel
fish.flavor: Winds itself around anchor lines and nets like it's helping. It is not helping.

fish.name: Grey Grunter
fish.flavor: Makes a low, disgruntled croak when landed. Honestly, fair enough.

fish.name: Halfmoon Porgy
fish.flavor: Silver as a coin and round as the moon it's named for. Catching one on your first cast is considered lucky; catching one on your last is considered showing off.

fish.name: Fog Pollock
fish.flavor: Appears when the visibility drops and vanishes with the sun. The fog does not explain itself, and neither does the pollock.

fish.name: Gullbait Smelt
fish.flavor: The gulls know your bucket has these in it before you do. Guard it with your hat if necessary.

fish.name: Tidesong Pilchard
fish.flavor: Schools so tightly it moves like one silver animal. On calm nights you can lean over the rail and hear the water hum with them.

fish.name: Copper Bonito
fish.flavor: Burns copper-bright in the sun and fights like it's twice its size. Frankly, it might be, and it's rude to check.

fish.name: Stormline Tuna
fish.flavor: Runs ahead of bad weather like a rumor. If you hook one, congratulations, and also secure everything you own.

fish.name: Lantern Jack
fish.flavor: Carries its own light through the black water, polite as a night watchman making rounds. Nods at passing anglers, or so the anglers insist.

fish.name: Preacher Haddock
fish.flavor: The dark blotch behind its head is said to be a thumbprint left by the sea itself. The haddock declines to comment.

fish.name: Widow's Ling
fish.flavor: Long, grim, and dressed head to tail for a funeral. Delicious, though, which complicates the mood at dinner.

fish.name: Sailor's Dorado
fish.flavor: Gold, green, and blue all at once, like the sea couldn't pick a favorite. Landing one is what sailors call a paid holiday.

fish.name: Barrel Amberjack
fish.flavor: Built like a barrel and pulls like a cart horse. Winning the argument takes both hands, one braced boot, and a word you'll apologize for later.

fish.name: Moonwake Garfish
fish.flavor: Skims the moonlit surface in long silver stitches, sewing your boat's wake back together behind you. Tidy little thing.

fish.name: Squallfin Trevally
fish.flavor: Its dorsal fin cuts the surface just before the wind picks up. Old skippers tip their caps to it and quietly reef the sails.

fish.name: Kettle Pomfret
fish.flavor: Round and dark as a kettle bottom, and somehow always caught right around teatime. Coincidence, say the pomfrets. All of them. In unison.

fish.name: Greybeard Wreckfish
fish.flavor: Haunts the old wrecks with a chin full of grey whiskers and several centuries of opinions. Locals say it remembers every ship it has outlived, and it has outlived all of them.

fish.name: Nine-Fathom Halibut
fish.flavor: Lives at exactly nine fathoms, no more, no less. Anglers who claim to have caught one at eight are measured with great suspicion.

fish.name: Weathervane Marlin
fish.flavor: Always found pointing into tomorrow's wind, accurate to the hour. The harbormasters have quietly stopped buying barometers.

fish.name: Ghostlight Herring
fish.flavor: One herring in ten thousand is born glowing. The school keeps it in the middle, like a candle carried carefully through a dark house.

fish.name: Bellringer Drum
fish.flavor: Booms through the hull like a chapel bell rung underwater. Some crews swear it tolls once for every year you've been fishing; new hands find this romantic, old hands find it loud.

fish.name: Milkeye Skate
fish.flavor: Pale eyes that have seen the bottom of everything. It glides under the boat slow as a passing thought, and takes about as long to let go of.

fish.name: Millstone Sunfish
fish.flavor: Big and round as a millstone and about as aerodynamic. Drifts sideways at the surface, sunning itself like it has earned the afternoon off. It has.

fish.name: Grandmother Gale
fish.flavor: The fishwives say every storm is just her turning over in her sleep, and every calm is her listening. She takes bait gently, the way you'd accept a gift from a child.

fish.name: The Drowned Lantern
fish.flavor: A cold green light rising out of the deep, swinging like a lamp carried to a doorway. Whatever it once guided home is long gone. Now it guides you.

fish.name: The Harbormaster's Regret
fish.flavor: An immense eel that circles the fleet's moorings once a year, always on the same date. Nobody in town remembers what happened on that date. The eel remembers.

fish.name: Saint Elmo's Herald
fish.flavor: Rides the bow-wave in the crackling minutes before lightning, fins fizzing with pale fire. Catching one is either a blessing or a warning, and it will not tell you which.

fish.name: Old Thunderhide
fish.flavor: The grandfather shark that every port along the coast claims as its own. Its hide carries a hundred harpoon stories, every one of which ends with the harpooner buying it a drink.

fish.name: King-o'-the-Herring
fish.flavor: A ribbon of silver and rose taller than your mast, said to lead the herring millions down their long winter road. To hold one is to feel the whole migration's heartbeat in your hands. Let it go.

fish.name: The Old Grey Under
fish.flavor: Every harbor has a story about the shadow that slides beneath the boats on windless days, longer than the fleet and quieter than the drowned. Hook it, and the whole sea holds its breath with you.
